absent: Translation entry payload layout and event to interrupt mapping beyond allocation and lookup.
Full register maps, control and status bit meanings and timing or ordering guarantees.
Device tree based translation unit discovery and other non firmware paths.
Interrupt domain callbacks, message handling, affinity migration and runtime power behavior.
Concurrency ordering between device allocation, table updates and cache maintenance.
Lifetime of lower level device table pages outside the teardown path shown.

findings.text: Per controller state keeps a device registry, an allocation mutex, a firmware handle, a cached device table configuration with alternative storage for flat versus hierarchical tables, a mapped register window, a flag word and message interrupt domain flags.

Per device state links to its parent controller, carries translation table configuration with flat versus hierarchical storage choice, a software event allocation map, a numeric device identifier, an event count and a translator base address.
Second level sizing uses nine index bits for small pages, eleven for medium pages and thirteen for large pages.
Support for second level page sizes is reported in three adjacent low identifier register positions, one per size, with the small size lowest.

Power of two helper shifts a 64 bit one by the given count; non coherent marker is the lowest flag bit; firmware described controller window spans sixty four kilobytes; driver log lines carry a fixed controller prefix.

Flat device table capacity grows as two raised to configured identifier width; when byte size would exceed the kernel allocation ceiling the width is reduced to fit with a warning; storage is zeroed and made visible before configuration and base registers are programmed and the configuration is cached.

Hierarchical device table splits identifier width into upper and lower portions derived from chosen second level size; upper table size is similarly capped with warning; upper entries are prefilled with span information and flushed before configuration and base registers are programmed and pointers are cached.

Table visibility depends on coherence flag: non coherent controllers require range clean to point of coherence while coherent controllers require only an ordering barrier; single entry updates combine one atomic store with the same maintenance.

Device entry lookup is direct indexing for flat tables and split high low indexing for hierarchical tables with optional on demand creation of missing lower tables and clamping of oversized span values; translation entry lookup follows the same flat versus split rule based on per device shape.

Controller enable and disable are symmetric operations that program the control enable bit and then wait for idle indication; cache synchronization waits for idle on a status register while device synchronization writes a sync register combining sync request and identifier then waits on a separate sync status.

Device bring up validates identifier against configured width, requires an unclaimed table slot, derives event identifier width from event count and checks it against hardware limit, builds flat or hierarchical translation storage, publishes a valid entry and invalidates caches with rollback to empty entry plus freed storage on invalidate failure; tear down requires a valid entry, clears it, frees storage and invalidates.

Flat translation storage allocates one entry per event identifier and records count and width; hierarchical storage rejects second level sizes covering the whole identifier space, sizes upper level from remaining bits, allocates lower tables sized by full width except possibly a smaller tail, publishes each lower table with address plus span plus valid marker, and frees lower tables before upper structures.

Single translation entry invalidate programs device, event and invalidate request registers then synchronizes; whole device invalidate programs device and device invalidate registers carrying event width and level selector then synchronizes.

Firmware affinity discovery runs per controller with current identifier and width derived from hardware register; only processors flagged enabled or online capable, matching the current controller, with resolvable logical index and affinity value inside width are bound to affinity and controller, others are skipped with warning when out of range.

Firmware controller discovery allocates per controller state, initializes the shared peripheral configuration lock, reserves and maps a fixed size window, records coherence mode and firmware region, establishes processor affinity, initializes hardware and announces shared peripheral range; failures unwind mapping, reservation, affinity and enable in reverse.

Device tree discovery walks available children of a parent, keeps only compatible controller nodes, attempts initialization per child and reports missing device when none remain; firmware discovery for both controller families parses the multiple APIC description table for their respective subtypes.
Global boot time entry points expose firmware table scans for both controller families and device tree scan for one family, with an empty fallback for one family when firmware support is absent.

Device allocation lock is a mutex embedded in per controller state; shared peripheral configuration changes are guarded by a raw spinlock embedded in per controller state and initialized during firmware discovery.

Interrupt domain setup creates a hierarchical parent domain using firmware handle, controller operations, domain flags and parent, plus a message interrupt info object linked back to the controller, freeing it on failure; informational logging reports controller name, table shape and identifier width derived from cached configuration.
Cached configuration word holds shape, sizing and width subfields accessed through a single field extractor; teardown selects flat versus hierarchical release based on extracted shape.

Allocation exhaustion, out of range identifiers, excessive event width, duplicate registration and oversized second level choice are reported as errors; identifier width reduction and overlapping firmware reservation produce warnings with continued or per controller degraded operation; this teardown path releases only upper device table structures.
